text:
Brayden Schenn is 35, a Stanley Cup winner and a former Blues captain, and on Long Island he has become exactly what the Islanders hoped: a veteran center who still produces. He has 11 points in 16 games at about 16:30 a night, with 38 hits, and the New York Post has written about him filling the leadership role and more.

The scoring is mostly honest. He's at five goals on 5.1 expected (the quality of his chances), so his finishing is right on line, and his on-ice results are fine. The one thing running warm is his shooting percentage, 17.2%, above where we'd expect it to settle. Our range has him finishing somewhere between 38 and 59 points, with about 48 the middle.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, so the bounce-back is real and worth noting. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows one quiet strength: 68% of his zone exits leave with possession. With Ryan Pulock, Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie out, the Islanders need every minute of that.
headline: Schenn is still doing the work
